text: hey everybody some claims about an ostensibly 1500 or 2 000 year old manuscript popped up again on Twitter
today and now I've been tagged a handful of times in a video sharing these claims check it out
now there are several problems with the notion that this is anything remotely approximating a 1500 or 2 000 year old
manuscript the first is that that claim that it's 1500 years old actually is
based on what that inscription on the bottom of the page actually says that's written in a language called Neo Assyrian it's related to Aramaic and
this inscription states that this text was written by monks in a high Monastery and Nineveh in the year of Our Lord
fifteen hundred so it claims to be from the year 1500 and that gets garbled and
turned into oh it's 1500 years old and then other people are saying or maybe even 2 000 years old just arbitrarily
there's no way it dates to the year 1500 there are two things about this inscription that make it clear this is a
modern forgery the first is that it is written in a script a style of letters associated with the neo-syrian language
that was not standardized until the late 19th century so the oldest it could possibly be is just over a century old
but there are also some odd and glaring spelling and grammar errors in the text it seems clear this was copied by
someone who does not actually know this language that all combines to suggest that this is something that was forged quite recently now this other claim that
this is somehow associated with the Gospel of Barnabas that was not a part of the original circulation of this manuscript and I've never seen any data
that indicate any relationship whatsoever with the Gospel of Barnabas and so I don't think that claim has any Merit whatsoever that's just something
that people have tacked on in order to provide some kind of content to what this book is supposed to be but I would
argue that this is a modern forgery probably no older than two or three decades
